content.comment_body: Good evening everyone. I'm experiencing issues with my ethernet cable, possibly due to its length but I'm not certain. I use a [product_name] module for garden irrigation, which is installed 20-25 meters from the router. Often, there is no connection. When I test it with a 1.5-meter cable at my desk, it works perfectly. Has anyone encountered this or know the cause? Thanks and apologies for my imperfect English.

I don't think the cable length is the root of the error. What is your module's firmware version? If you have firmware version [version_no] and your [product_name] module includes a display, there may be a non-repairable error that requires device replacement.

You may be correct. My module has a display and when attempting firmware connection, the attached file appears. Could Windows 10 be causing this issue? I've heard that users sometimes need to downgrade to Windows 8 for proper operation.
That seems like a different error.

It's strange. Locally, I can access and use the page I created with [product_name] panel, but I can't connect with the software to modify the program. I also can't retrieve the firmware version. Thanks [user_name].
[product_name] programming software V8.0 does not support Windows 10. Do you have version V8.1? It's released for Windows 10. Also, is your Java installation up-to-date?

I'm fairly certain I updated, but now I'm downloading the latest version. Hopefully that will solve the issue. Otherwise, I may need to purchase a new module. Thanks so much for the support, I might reach out again if I have more questions.
I don't think purchasing a new module is your only option. Can you connect to the [product_name] with only the short cable? And does everything work as expected with the short cable?

Yes, I can connect using both short and long cables, although the long cable currently isn't working. For now, I can't transfer data from the module to my PC or modify the program's structure, so I'm using the short cable.

Is it possible you have the newer [product_name] version [version_no]? If so, review the [company_name] FAQ, which explains how to find your module's housing version. It also addresses issues related to downloading programs into the new hardware.
[article_no] is the model referenced by [company_name].
That's an order number from [company_name] for a specific module type [article_no]. Multiple firmware versions share the same order number.

Alright, [user_name], I have re-installed version 8.1. On the diagrams page, the lower right showed the version you mentioned, FS4. I switched to [version_no] and now it works—data transfer and reading is possible. My initial problem remains, though. I plan to try an ethernet switch to improve signal quality. Do you think this could help?
An Ethernet switch simply routes one input to several outputs. What concerns do you have specifically?

By the way, I don't have the newest version; I've been using this one since October. Changing the name at the bottom of the software window resolved the communication problem. The firmware version is: [version_no] V1.08.02.

Your mistake was leaving the default setting as the new [product_name] version [version_no]. Changing the device selection to '[version_no]' fixed it. It happens. The main thing is that it's working now.
I don't have concerns about the module itself, but my issue is still with the long cable—it doesn't work. You mentioned a firmware version I don't have; based on your experience, should I upgrade?
And [user_name], thank you for your assistance, especially this late in the evening.

Unfortunately, the module's firmware can't be updated. New firmware only comes with purchasing a newer module. The current model is [version_no] with firmware FW V1.81.01. For this, you need the latest programming software V8.1. For older [version_no] modules, you don't need the new software.
Good to know. Thanks again! Time to get some rest.
Hello [user_name], you're welcome. I had a good night's sleep.

Have you tested another network-capable device on the long cable, such as a printer? It's possible the cable is faulty. Placing a switch near the [product_name] could help with distance, since a switch not only connects devices but also amplifies the signal. However, the [product_name] manual states network cables can be up to 100 meters, matching Ethernet specs, so a switch may not be necessary for a 25-meter cable.

Ethernet cables should not exceed 100 meters, and only three routers or switches should be connected in series. So length likely isn't the issue, but with longer cables, higher quality is important—something I've learned from networking experience.

I'm having similar issues. I ordered the following item: [url]. I'll update if it helps. I'm using [product_name] to control pool, spa, heat exchangers, and HVAC units. If others are interested, I can share my pool setup ideas.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing connectivity problems between their PC and [product_name] hardware when using a longer Ethernet cable (20-25m), whereas a short cable (1.5m) works reliably. The issue is evident in failures to transfer data or modify programs, with questions around whether the cause is cable length, firmware compatibility, operating system support, or software version mismatches. Suggestions from others shift focus away from cable length and point toward firmware, hardware version, and software compatibility concerns.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable and consistent connectivity between their PC and [product_name] hardware independent of Ethernet cable length, particularly for data transfer and program modification. They also anticipate compatibility with current operating systems.
